newsitem.title: USA: Parking meter granny fined but not jailed.
newsitem.headline: Parking meter granny fined but not jailed.

text.p: A 63-year-old grandmother's 15-cent good deed of putting coins in other people's parking meters will cost her $500 plus court costs, but she will not do any jail time, a judge said on Monday.
Sylvia Stayton was convicted in Cincinnati last month by an eight-member jury of obstructing official business. The jury acquitted her of a more serious charge of disorderly conduct.
Stayton was unrepentant about the Oct. 24 incident or about prolonging her case through six court sessions.
"I would not offer any apology (in court) when I know in my heart of hearts that I did nothing wrong," Stayton told reporters after her sentencing. She also said she will appeal the sentence.

Judge John A. West of Hamilton County Municipal Court in Cincinnati could have sentenced her to 90 days in jail but prosecutors asked only that she be fined. She had been jailed briefly at the time of her arrest last fall.
Stayton, mother of four and grandmother of 10, had been on an errand involving the foreclosure of her home when she saw a policeman about to ticket two cars.
He said she defied his order not to feed the meters. She put a nickel in one meter and a dime in the other.
She denied Assistant Prosecutor Ernie McAdams's allegation that she rejected a plea bargain because she was seeking the worldwide publicity her case received.
